newsitem.title: USA: U.S. critical of detention of Congo politician.
newsitem.headline: U.S. critical of detention of Congo politician.

text.p: The United States criticised on Friday the overnight detention of Congolese opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi and repeated that international aid to the new government hinged on respect for democratic norms.

"We would report that the record continues to be mixed," State Department spokesman John Dinger told a regular press briefing when asked about the detention of Tshisekedi, a thorn in the side first of ousted dictator Mobutu Sese Seko and now of Laurent Kabila, new president of the former Zaire.

The United States has welcomed Kabila's promise to hold elections in April 1999 and the specific timetable he has set. Kabila grabbed power in May and renamed the country the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

"At the same time, banning political party activity and public rallies and this latest development is certainly negative," Dinger said. "We have to emphasise that free political activity will be essential as the Congo embarks on its democratic transition."

Soldiers detained Tshisekedi, head of the Union for Democracy and Social Progress, after he defied a ban to address a political gathering Thursday. He was released after questioning on Friday along with members of his family and associates who also had been held.

Kabila has banned political parties and gatherings and has alienated opposition followers by excluding Tshisekedi from his new government. The ban has undermined support for Kabila, who was a hero for ending Mobutu's corrupt 32-year rule.
Dinger reiterated the U.S. position that aid from the international community would depend to a large extent on Kabila's actions on political issues as well as his human rights performance.
